title.text: Apply test eligibility and vision rules

why_how.text: An applicant must be at least fifteen to take the knowledge and skills tests.
The minimum vision standard is twenty-forty in at least one eye, with corrective lenses permitted.
Using glasses or contacts for the vision screening results in a lens restriction on the license.
A driver with a lens restriction must wear the required glasses or contacts whenever driving.
Ignoring the required lens restriction can lead to a citation and suspension of driving privileges.
A county DMV agent may require a physician’s medical form before licensing when a condition could affect safe driving.
A new applicant, an other-state transfer or a holder whose Idaho license expired at least twenty-five months must take the knowledge test.

result.text: Choose “Twenty-forty in at least one eye, with corrective lenses permitted”. Keep the setting and every stated condition attached to that response.

correction.text: The minimum vision standard is twenty-forty in at least one eye, with corrective lenses permitted.

why_how.text: To change the credential name, an applicant must request a duplicate or make the change during an eligible renewal.
A credential name change requires legal evidence such as an Idaho-standard certified marriage record, a court-certified divorce decree or court documents.
Before applying for a duplicate to show a changed name, update the name with the Social Security Administration.
A change of address must be reported to ITD within thirty days.
A changed address appears on the physical credential only after a duplicate application or eligible renewal.
The driving record must contain the actual physical address even when a different mailing address is used.
An Idaho or other-state Class D license expired at least twenty-five months requires the applicable knowledge and skills tests.
If a lost driver license or identification card is found after a duplicate has been issued, the old document must be destroyed or surrendered to the county license office.

why_how.text: The knowledge and skills tests may be taken in either order.
Skills tests may be scheduled only during daylight and acceptable weather.
Twelve or fewer errors is the skills-test passing score.
A failed skills test requires a three-day wait before retesting.
A skills-test retake requires paying both the county and examiner fees again.
A critical driving error automatically fails the skills test and ends it immediately.
Missing the same scored skill five or more times is a critical driving error.
Parking more than eighteen inches from the curb while impeding traffic is a critical driving error.

why_how.text: A skills-test applicant must bring photo identity evidence, such as a state-issued photo identification card or driver license, an instruction or supervised instruction permit, a passport, a school identification card or a yearbook.
A non-owner using a vehicle for testing must give the examiner the owner’s written permission or permission spoken in person.
Permission to use the test vehicle cannot be given over the telephone.
The test vehicle must carry current insurance evidence on paper or in digital form.
An SR22 does not qualify as skills-test proof of insurance.
The test vehicle must carry current registration signed by the registrant, rather than a photocopy.
A skills-test receipt is required for identity verification only when no state-issued credential is supplied, and photo identification is still necessary.

why_how.text: Before the skills test, the examiner checks the passenger door and seatbelt, required mirrors, windshield, tires and dashboard indicators against Idaho and ITD standards.
Skills-test tires must have at least two thirty-seconds of an inch of tread.

A newcomer who has lost a valid other-state driver license or identification card must provide documentation to help verify identity.

why_how.text: A person who has never been licensed must take a skills test.
A learner younger than seventeen who completed approved training and supervised instruction must take the skills test when eligible.
An instruction-permit holder aged seventeen or older needs a skills test to become licensed.
An applicant whose vision does not meet the minimum standard must take a skills test.
A recurring skills-test requirement may result from a medical or vision condition.
A foreign-license applicant must take a skills test unless a reciprocity agreement applies.
A non-commercial Idaho or other-state license expired at least twenty-five months requires a skills test.
A skills test is required for an applicant with a mental or physical impairment that might affect safe vehicle operation.
A skills test is required when a county agent has concerns about an applicant's ability to drive safely, regardless of prior licensing, experience or age.
Third-party contractors administer Idaho’s Class D skills tests.
An applicant needing or wanting a restricted skills test must notify the examiner.
A restricted skills test is for an applicant unable to drive outside existing or proposed restrictions, or an applicant who wants to drive only between specified locations.
An applicant seeking an unrestricted license must complete the whole test route without modifications.
An applicant considering a restricted skills test must discuss the options with the examiner before taking the test.
If applicable, an applicant with a medical-caution reevaluation or skills-test requirement must bring ITD's Skills Test Evaluation Form to the skills test.
Skills-test passengers are normally prohibited, and each permitted exception passenger must be at least eighteen, carry valid identification and sign the liability waiver.
One parent or legal guardian may accompany a skills-test applicant aged seventeen or younger if the passenger is at least eighteen, has valid identification and signs the liability waiver.

A translator may accompany a skills-test applicant without translator certification or a driver license if the translator is at least eighteen, has valid identification and signs the liability waiver.
The applicant is responsible for obtaining a translator when one is needed for the skills test.
A law-enforcement officer may accompany a current inmate during a skills test if the officer is at least eighteen, has valid identification and signs the liability waiver.
When requested, a religious missionary companion may accompany the skills-test applicant if the companion is at least eighteen, has valid identification and signs the liability waiver.
The skills test includes business and residential roads, curves, freeway driving, lane changes, parking lots, left and right turns, U-turns and stall and curb parking.
Skills-test scoring includes vehicle control, observation, spacing, signaling, speed, stopping, lane position, parking and right of way.
Controlled and uncontrolled intersections, railroad crossings and roundabouts are included in the skills test.
A dangerous action during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Disobeying an emergency or safety vehicle during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Disobeying police or safety personnel during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Disregarding a traffic sign or signal during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Driving onto a curb or sidewalk during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Examiner intervention or disobedience to the examiner during the skills test is a critical driving error.
A lane violation during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Passenger interference during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Speeding during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Striking an object during the skills test is a critical driving error.
The skills-test windshield must have no cracks or obstructions.
The test vehicle must have a rear-view mirror or both side mirrors.
Critical dashboard warning lights or gauges must not be illuminated on the skills-test vehicle.
The handbook warns that online practice tests do not accurately represent Idaho knowledge tests, apart from ITD’s own website sample questions.
